class.name: GameMode
class.brief_description: Per-level rules object that logs players in, spawns them and possesses their pawns.
class.description: Created from [GameModeSettings] - either the [Level] override or [code]application/game_framework/default_game_mode_settings[/code] - and destroyed with the level. There are two moments to work with. [code]_init_game[/code] runs before the level's nodes have started - they exist and are reachable, but have not run [code]_enter_tree[/code] or [code]_ready[/code] - for every level opened with [method GFGDSceneTree.open_level]; the first level is the main scene, which Godot has already added, so there its nodes have run [code]_ready[/code] first. The game mode's own [code]_ready[/code] is the other: the framework adds it to the tree after the level, so by then the level, its nodes and the players have all started. Prepare in [code]_init_game[/code], play in [code]_ready[/code]. Spawning is the framework's job. Return [code]false[/code] from [code]_init_game[/code], or do not override it at all, and every [LocalPlayer] is logged in and possessed before the level enters the tree - which is what makes the players reachable from every node's [code]_ready[/code], including nodes authored into the level. Reach them through the world: [method GFGDSceneTree.get_first_player_controller] and [method GFGDSceneTree.get_player_controllers]. Return [code]true[/code] to suppress that entirely. That is how a menu level runs with no player at all, rather than with an empty one. [b]It owns the rules, not the facts.[/b] Conceptually this is the server's object: it decides who may join and where they spawn. Anything every peer is meant to see - the player list, the score - belongs on the [GameState], which is why that is a separate node created by [GFGDSceneTree]. [method login] refuses to run without authority, so code written against it stays correct once there is networking. For the same reason the game mode holds no player controller of its own. The world does, as [method GFGDSceneTree.get_first_player_controller] and [method GFGDSceneTree.get_player_controllers] - a client has those and no game mode at all.

method.name: _can_join
method.description: Return [code]false[/code] to refuse a press-to-join from this device. This is where "two pads only, ignore the keyboard" belongs: [codeblock] func _can_join(device_slot: int) -> bool: return device_slot != PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_KEYBOARD_MOUSE [/codeblock]

method.name: _choose_player_start
method.description: Return the node to place this controller's pawn at, or [code]null[/code] to use the default search.

method.name: _init_game
method.description: Return [code]true[/code] if you handled player spawning yourself, [code]false[/code] to let the framework log everyone in.

method.name: _on_post_login
method.description: Runs after the controller, its [PlayerState] and its pawn all exist. The place to name the player or set up per-player HUD.

method.name: _spawn_default_pawn_for
method.description: Return a spawned pawn to take pawn creation over entirely, or [code]null[/code] to use [method spawn_default_pawn_for].

method.name: choose_player_start
method.description: Picks an unclaimed node whose name starts with [code]PlayerStart[/code], searching the level recursively. A glob rather than a class, so a level with one node called [code]PlayerStart[/code] keeps working and [code]PlayerStart2[/code] is picked up for free. Claims are per level. With more players than starts the framework warns and reuses them by player index - it cannot test for an occupied start, because the level is deliberately still outside the tree when the first players spawn and physics is not available there.

method.name: get_player_controllers
method.description: Every [PlayerController] in the world, from [method GFGDSceneTree.get_player_controllers].

method.name: login
method.description: Creates the [PlayerController] and [PlayerState] for a local player, then restarts it. Returns the existing controller if the player already has one.

method.name: logout
method.description: Frees the pawn, the [PlayerState] and the controller. The [LocalPlayer] survives - it belongs to the [GameInstance].

method.name: restart_all_players
method.description: Logs in every [LocalPlayer] that has no controller, up to [member GameModeSettings.max_local_players]. Creates the implicit first player if the project has never made one, which is what makes an untouched single player project behave as it always did.

method.name: restart_player
method.description: Spawns a fresh pawn at a chosen start and possesses it.

method.name: spawn_default_pawn_for
method.description: Instantiates the pawn scene for this player - [method GameModeSettings.get_pawn_scene_for_player] - and places it at [method choose_player_start].

method.name: spawn_default_player
method.description: Ensures local player 0 exists, logs it in and returns its controller. Kept for projects written against the single player API.

method.name: try_join
method.description: Called by the [InputRouter] when a button is pressed on a device no player owns. Honours [member GameModeSettings.allow_press_to_join], [member GameModeSettings.max_local_players] and [method _can_join]. A player who is already in the game but has no device claims the slot first, so this doubles as "press a button to pick your pad back up" after a disconnect.

signal.name: player_restarted
signal.description: Emitted every time a player gets a fresh pawn, including respawns.
